subject: HemLogic — post‑signature phased cutover, canary lanes and training windows
messages:
From: sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@hemlogic.com>, Samir Desai <samir.desai@hemlogic.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: HemLogic — post‑signature phased cutover, canary lanes and training windows

Hi Nina / Samir —

Congrats again on signing — excited to get the HemLogic rollout moving. Attached is our initial MAP spreadsheet (HemLogic‑MAP‑v1) with a proposed timeline that embeds implementation tasks directly into the MAP so we can track sign‑offs and acceptance criteria week‑by‑week. High level plan: 

Phase A — Prep & Configuration (Week 0–2)
- Account provisioning + secrets/KMS handoff
- Baseline test dataset ingest (non‑prod)
- Access matrix for primary users

Phase B — Canary (Week 3)
- 2 small canary cohorts (5–10% traffic) on dedicated nodes
- Canary success criteria: latency < 200ms p95, no regression on the 10 prompt evals, and zero data exfil alerts
- Auto rollback triggers and a manual hold gate

Phase C — Gradual Migration (Weeks 4–6)
- Traffic ramp to 50% then 100% across two waves
- Parallel training sessions (train‑the‑trainer + recorded modules)

Phase D — Full Acceptance / Handover (Week 7)
- Final eval run, acceptance sign‑off, transfer runbook to HemLogic ops

Requests from our side: please confirm which engineering SMEs will own the acceptance criteria sign‑off, and whether the week‑3 canary window (proposed June 17–21) works for your team. I included a tentative training calendar (training‑calendar.ics) and the canary checklist.

Next steps:
- If you approve the timeline we’ll lock dates in HubSpot and schedule a kickoff demo + runbook review.
- Ben will follow up with procurement items once you confirm the first training window.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if useful.

—Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555‑0192

Cc: Samir Desai <samir.desai@hemlogic.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 May 2029 10:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: HemLogic — post‑signature phased cutover, canary lanes and training windows

Sofia — thanks for the clear plan and congrats to the team. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Training windows: the proposed week of June 17 conflicts with our quarterly release freeze. Can we push the canary to June 24–28? We can still do kickoff prep the week prior.

2) Acceptance owners: I’ll own the business acceptance sign‑off (Nina), Samir will be technical acceptance. Procurement (procure@hemlogic.com) is CC’d here for contract milestone billing info.

3) Canary cohort sizing: 5–10% seems right for the first cohort; prefer 2 separate cohorts on different regions to validate routing policies.

I reviewed the MAP spreadsheet and left a couple of inline comments on the Drive link (see your related links). Once we align dates Ben, we’ll confirm purchase order timing.

—Nina
Nina Patel
Director, Product Operations — HemLogic
Nina.Patel@hemlogic.com
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: nina.patel <nina.patel@hemlogic.com>, sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2029 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HemLogic — post‑signature phased cutover, canary lanes and training windows

Nina / Sofia — technical notes from implementation engineering: 

• Canary design: agree with two cohorts split by region (us‑west / us‑east). We’ll deploy separate canary pools and route a controlled percentage via traffic‑shaping rules.

• Acceptance criteria (technical):
  - p95 latency < 200ms (observed at 95th over 1h window)
  - Token accuracy regression < 2% across our eval set (we’ll run the eval harness included in MAP)
  - KV cache miss rate baseline established in Phase A

• Rollback plan: immediate route back to baseline model variant + pause autoscale if CPU/GPU error rate > 3% over 10m. Vivek will own the technical rollback checklist during the canary window.

I added a short canary checklist (canary‑checklist.pdf) and an infra task list into the shared Drive. If HemLogic wants a dry‑run (no traffic, just smoke tests) we can schedule that on June 10–11. Dry‑run strongly recommended.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@hemlogic.com>, sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 4 Jun 2029 14:36:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: HemLogic — post‑signature phased cutover, canary lanes and training windows

Nina — appreciate the quick review and the procurement loop.

Per Nina’s note we’ll move the canary week to June 24–28. Proposed next milestones (updated in HubSpot):
- 2029‑06‑10: dry‑run smoke test (no traffic) — infra team and HemLogic SMEs
- 2029‑06‑17: final runbook review + train‑the‑trainer session (recorded)
- 2029‑06‑24–28: Canary week (two cohorts, us‑west/us‑east)
- 2029‑07‑08: Full migration wave 1 (50% traffic)
- 2029‑07‑22: Full migration complete + handover

I’ll open the PO milestone in the contract and tag procure@hemlogic.com. HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/987654321 — I also added the PO milestone and acceptance checklist.

Ok to lock these dates, Nina? If so I’ll create calendar invites and a 30‑minute kickoff on June 6 to walk the runbook.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: HemLogic — post‑signature phased cutover, canary lanes and training windows

Thanks — dates look good and we approve the adjusted timeline. Please schedule the June 6 kickoff and send the calendar invites (I’ll ensure our SME availability). Procurement acknowledges the PO milestone and will look for the DocuSign envelope.

Nina (final sign‑off on timeline)
